## Overview

RLMADJ06 addresses #409 D2 by asking **which measured skills go with more word-reading progress across successive annual transitions** in the Byrne cohort. It stacks waves 1→2, 2→3, 3→4 and 4→5 rather than reducing each child to the waves-1→3 span used by RLMADJ01. BAS word reading at each post wave is conditioned on its own pre-wave level and the mutually adjusted pre-wave levels of BPVS receptive vocabulary (`bpvs`), TROG receptive grammar (`trog`), BAS digit recall (`basdig`), BAS similarities (`bassim`) and age. All six measurement inputs have confirmed instrument identities and ceilings.

_Adjusted longitudinal associations only._ Temporal ordering does not make the slopes causal. Stable unmeasured differences can still confound the predictor–outcome relationship, and the child random intercept is a partial-pooling representation of stable heterogeneity rather than a fixed-effect control that removes it. Every coefficient is therefore an adjusted association (`causal_status="none"`), not an effect of changing a skill.

_Comparable within-transition scale._ Each bounded predictor is Haldane-logit transformed and every predictor, including age, is standardised separately within each transition. The pooled slope therefore compares children one transition-specific standard deviation apart at their current wave; it is not driven by average score growth between waves. Separate transition intercepts absorb the mean developmental trajectory.

_Wave-5 scope condition._ The first three transitions include all three observational reading groups, whereas wave 5 is available only for the Down syndrome cohort. The four-transition pooled fit is retained because it is the declared panel extension, but it cannot by itself establish that the same profile generalises to the other cohorts at that age. A common-horizon sensitivity drops the waves-4→5 tail, and a transition-specific-slope sensitivity shows how weakly the small final cell identifies its own coefficients.

## Model

For child $i$ in transition $j$, with transition-start word-reading logit $b_{ij}$ and within-transition-standardised predictors $z_{k,ij}$:

$$
y_{ij} \sim \mathrm{BetaBinomial}(90,\ p_{ij},\ \kappa),
\qquad
\operatorname{logit}(p_{ij}) = \alpha_j + \gamma_{\text{own}} b_{ij} +
\textstyle\sum_k \beta_k z_{k,ij} + \boldsymbol{\beta}_{\text{grp}}^{\top}
\mathbf{d}_{ij} + u_i,
\qquad
u_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0,\sigma_{\text{child}}).
$$

Here $y_{ij}$ is the post-wave BAS word-reading count (confirmed ceiling 90), $\beta_k \sim \mathrm{Normal}(0,0.3)$ are the pooled annual per-SD associations, and the group dummies are nuisance terms. Child-level PSIS-LOO sums the likelihood over all observed transitions for a child before leaving that child out. The bivariate comparisons retain the own baseline, transition, group and child structure; the prior-width sensitivity uses slope standard deviations 0.5 and 0.7 and widens the own-baseline coupling prior $\gamma_{\text{own}} \sim \mathrm{Normal}(1, 0.25)$ to SD 0.5. The Beta-Binomial concentration takes the dispersion-scale prior of the Byrne historical families, $1/\sqrt{\kappa} \sim \mathrm{HalfNormal}(0.25)$, so the near-Binomial limit is not excluded a priori (2026-08-22 adjusted-family review). The items-scale contrasts are averaged over the fitted transition rows with the child intercept at zero. The transition-specific sensitivity replaces each pooled $\beta_k$ with four independently estimated transition coefficients under the same prior and is descriptive only.
